title: A meta-analytic comparison of eye movement subtypes as potential biomarkers of schizophrenia
title_zh: 眼动亚型作为精神分裂症潜在生物标志物的元分析比较
abstract: Schizophrenia is a complex psychiatric disorder characterized by significant cognitive and perceptual dysfunctions, including disturbances in eye movements such as saccades, smooth pursuit, and fixations. These oculomotor abnormalities have been increasingly studied as potential biomarkers for schizophrenia. However, previous studies have been limited by inconsistent findings and methodological variability. More specifically, to date, literature lacks a direct comparison of the main types of eye movements and their relative metrics (e.g., number of fixations) with respect to the main brain function involved in each one (e.g., attention, memory). The present pre-registered meta-analysis overcomes these limitations by using data from 211 studies, comprising 539 samples, for a total of 9675 schizophrenia patients and 12086 healthy controls. Results highlighted antisaccades error rate, indexing inhibitory control capacity, as the most effective and precise for distinguishing schizophrenia patients from controls, thus indicating this eye movement as a putative biomarker for schizophrenia. Scanpath length during free-viewing tasks, indexing global visual scanning ability, was identified as the second-best candidate. By providing a comprehensive, quantitative evaluation, this study advances understanding of eye movement dysfunction in schizophrenia and aids the development of more objective diagnostic tools and treatment strategies. Data and other relevant materials are available at https://osf.io/jr9qs/.
abstract_zh: 精神分裂症是一种复杂的精神疾病，其特征为显著的认知和知觉功能障碍，包括眼动障碍（如跳跃运动、平滑追踪和注视）。这些眼动异常越来越多地被研究作为精神分裂症的潜在生物标志物。然而，以往的研究结果不一且方法学差异较大。具体而言，现有文献缺乏对主要眼动类型及其相关度量（例如，注视次数）与涉及各类眼动的主要脑功能（例如，注意、记忆）的直接比较。本预注册元分析利用来自211项研究、共539个样本、涉及9675名精神分裂症患者和12086名健康对照的数据，克服了上述局限性。结果表明，反映抑制控制能力的抗冲动眼动错误率在区分精神分裂症患者与对照组方面最为有效且精确，表明该眼动可作为精神分裂症的潜在生物标志物。自由观察任务中的扫视路径长度，反映全局视觉扫描能力，被确定为第二优先候选指标。通过提供全面、定量的评估，本研究促进了对精神分裂症眼动功能障碍的理解，并有助于开发更客观的诊断工具和治疗策略。数据及其他相关材料可在 https://osf.io/jr9qs/ 获取。
